items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: I feel really honored having had the opportunity of working with guys like that. And of course I really enjoyed working with Al Hurd and Pete Fountain... the late Harry Shields

ctx.x: Oh sure, well I knew Monk. He was the first jazz musician in New Orleans that I ever got to know was Monk. And that was when he was working on Broadway in the Alcohol Factory. Right. Walking around in it all day long.

You know Dick, I really feel very good of having had the opportunity of working with fellas like the late Monk Hable, the late Larry Shields, and Jeff Riddick, and the late Almond Hug. Which Shields? Larry Shields. Harry Shields.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: It must have been Harry Shields, I guess. Yeah, Harry Shields on clarinet... We were doing two shows a night in Chicago... he just flipped over old Harry Shields... He loved Harry Shields.

ctx.x: Did you say who the clarinet player was? Oh, uh... Start at the top. The high note.

It must have been Harry Shields, I guess. Yeah, Harry Shields on clarinet. The late Harry Shields. And uh, Les Sharky on trumpet. Now let's see who am I leaving out. Joe Rodas trombone. Monk Hazel drums. Piano? We only had six men. I'm trying to think. Oh, Harvey Rubin. Harvey Rubin. Oh, yeah? Yeah, Harvey Rubin was on piano. Because he traveled in his little Volkswagen. He always had a Volkswagen in those days.
